analyst.summary: Shriram Finance had a strong FY26: profit crossed ₹10,000 crore for the first time, the loan book crossed ₹3 lakh crore, and Japan's MUFG Bank completed a large ₹39,618 crore investment for a 20% stake that pushed the company's capital position and credit ratings to the top of the industry (AAA across all major agencies), which should lower its borrowing costs over the next two years. At the same time, the share of loans showing early repayment stress has crept up for two straight quarters across used-vehicle, MSME and personal-loan segments, even though the company has also built up a bigger cushion against losses. The stock has already re-rated sharply over the past year on the MUFG and rating-upgrade news, so at current levels we see it as fairly valued rather than a bargain. We rate it a Hold: a genuinely stronger balance sheet, but not enough margin of safety at this price to add, and the recent rise in early-stress loans is worth watching, not ignoring.
